heading: Projects
intro: What each one solves, how it's built and where it falls short.

projects.title: Calgary Transit Live
projects.summary: Calgary's realtime bus feed, joined to the schedule and played back on a live map.
projects.problem: Bus positions arrive bare: no route, no stops. Joining them to the static schedule makes them readable on a map.
projects.architecture: Calgary feeds → Python poller → PostgreSQL → Express API → React/Leaflet map. A live dashboard reads the same tables.
pipeline: Poll three realtime feeds from 08:00 to 21:00
Keep current state plus a short position history
Join trips to routes, shapes, stops and alerts in PostgreSQL
Play buses back slightly delayed, along their own route shape
outcomes: Web, API and poller deployed as separate services on one database
Keeps source timestamps and marks stopped and stale buses
Route picker, upcoming stops and alerts
limitations: The CTrain feed has no confirmed vehicle positions yet
Playback is deliberately delayed, not an exact live location
Alert display still needs a real alert from the feed to confirm

lab.heading: Build notes

techniques.title: Sparse-feed enrichment
techniques.concept: Realtime records become useful when stable identifiers connect them to slower-changing reference data.
techniques.implementation: VehiclePositions supplies trip IDs and coordinates; PostgreSQL joins those trip IDs to static GTFS routes, shapes, stops, and service calendars before the API shapes a frontend response.
techniques.tradeoff: The join produces richer context without inventing data, but schedule-version drift can leave some realtime trips unmatched and must remain visible as a data-quality condition.

techniques.title: Delayed interpolation
techniques.concept: A small playback buffer can make discrete observations readable without pretending to predict the future.
techniques.implementation: The browser plays approximately 45 seconds behind the source and interpolates only between two observed positions, while stale and stopped thresholds preserve source honesty.
techniques.tradeoff: The map looks smoother and remains evidence-based, but it is intentionally delayed and cannot claim exact instantaneous vehicle location.

techniques.title: Independent feed transactions
techniques.concept: Related upstream feeds can have different failure modes, so one bad payload should not discard valid sibling updates.
techniques.implementation: Vehicle positions, trip updates, and alerts each own a transaction inside one polling cycle; failures roll back and log only the affected feed.
techniques.tradeoff: Useful partial freshness survives an upstream problem, while health reporting must disclose that the resulting snapshot may span different source times.

techniques.title: Freshness as a service contract
techniques.concept: An HTTP 200 and a database connection do not prove that a realtime product has current data.
techniques.implementation: The health endpoint reports source timestamps, recent vehicle counts, operating hours, and healthy, degraded, or expected after-hours states.
techniques.tradeoff: Monitoring and users receive an honest state, but thresholds and operating schedules become explicit operational configuration that must be maintained.

lab.working_method: Codex was used as an AI-assisted development tool. The portfolio owner reviewed and validated the resulting work.

projects.title: Canada Rates Pipeline
projects.summary: Bank of Canada rates loaded into PostgreSQL and modelled with dbt for a rates page.
projects.problem: Policy rate, CORRA, bond yields and USD/CAD come from one public API in different shapes. They need one tested daily table before anything can chart them.
projects.architecture: Bank of Canada Valet API → Python loader → raw schema → dbt staging and marts → rates page.
pipeline: Upsert new observations and log every run
Model staging, a fact table and a daily mart in dbt
Test the models and check source freshness
outcomes: Re-runnable loads with a run log
Tested dbt models with documented lineage
Read-only rates page with charts and a rate-decision log
limitations: The production reporting database comes in the next stage, so the live rates page has no data yet
Daily values only, as the Bank publishes them
